title: Check yourself: The support agent: the scenario, its layers and the first fix

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A month of support-agent sessions shows two problems: in 3 percent a refund was issued before the customer was identified, and in 9 percent the agent escalated cases that policy lets it settle. Which fix is made first?

options.text: Train a separate model on past tickets first, so it can decide which cases need a person
options.says: Ruled out because a trained model comes before words were tried: "machinery for a problem nobody has tried to fix with words".

options.text: Write escalation criteria first, because that problem touches the larger share of sessions
options.says: Ruled out because the size of a count does not set the order: "The first fix goes to what cannot be undone."

options.text: Rewrite the descriptions of the tools first, since both problems start with tool choice
options.says: Ruled out because the skipped step is a step order and not a tool choice: "A step order that is only requested".

options.text: Enforce the call sequence in the dispatcher, because moved money cannot be recalled
options.says: Money that moved wrongly cannot be called back, so its cause is fixed first.

origin.section: Money before rate, and the proportionate fix before the large one

questions.stem: A customer asks about a purchase that belongs to someone else. How does the support example's dispatcher refuse the call?

options.text: As `order_not_owned`, and the message does not name the owner
options.says: The refusal is `order_not_owned` and keeps the owner out of it: "An order that belongs to someone else is refused as `order_not_owned`, and the message does not say whose it is."

options.text: As `order_not_owned`, and the message names the owner of the order
options.says: Ruled out by the same sentence: "the message does not say whose it is".

options.text: As `not_found`, and the message says that the order does not exist
options.says: Ruled out because `not_found` is the answer of the identity step: "No match returns `not_found` with the same advice."

options.text: As `needs_human`, and the message tells the model to escalate
options.says: Ruled out because that refusal belongs to the amount: "above it the refusal is `needs_human`, which tells the model that the next step is to escalate".

questions.stem: Two customers share a name, the lookup tool returns both, and the agent proceeds with the first. What should the dispatcher have done?

options.text: Choose the customer whose order is the most recent one on file
options.says: Ruled out because the dispatcher does not pick: "Several matches set nothing and return the refusal".

options.text: Verify both customers, and let either be served as the case unfolds
options.says: Ruled out because the desk holds one verified customer, set only by a single match: "One match sets the verified customer."

options.text: Set nobody as verified, and have the model ask what tells them apart
options.says: Several matches are a question for the customer, and nothing is set.

options.text: Raise the retry count of the lookup until it returns one match
options.says: Ruled out because the refusal is not a fault that a retry can clear: "A retryable error (a timeout of the order service) is retried once by the loop, which is the loop's business, not the model's."
